sourceScope: Peer-reviewed 2021 stream trophic study and 2022 original Kampalili mammal account.
policy: No bait-as-diet claim, no generalized locality inference or precise rare-species coordinates.

records.label: Northeast Mindanao stream-food study
records.text: Stomach contents and stable-isotope analyses from a northeast Mindanao stream study supported generalist feeding on locally available invertebrate prey in the sampled Limnonectes magnus.
records.source: Plaza, Metillo & Sanguila (2021), Journal of Tropical Ecology 37
records.sourceLocation: Abstract; trophic comparisons among seven stream-associated frogs
records.studyScope: Seven sympatric frog species from low- and mid-elevation streams of one northeast Mindanao watershed; the inferred trophic niche is not a nationwide diet or prey-availability estimate.

records.label: Opportunistic insect consumption
records.text: The local stable-isotope estimates characterized Limnonectes magnus as an opportunistic generalist consuming locally abundant insect prey in the sampled stream community.
records.source: Plaza, Metillo & Sanguila (2021), Journal of Tropical Ecology 37
records.sourceLocation: Abstract; stable-isotope analysis of locally sampled stream frogs
records.studyScope: Study-specific diet interpretation for a sampled northeast Mindanao riparian community, not direct verification of every prey species or a permanent species-wide feeding preference.

records.label: Original moss-covered log microhabitats
records.text: Two originally collected animals were captured under or beside moss-covered fallen logs on a steep upper-montane forest slope with deep humus and abundant shrubs and epiphytes.
records.source: Rowsey et al. (2022), Journal of Mammalogy 103:1259–1277
records.sourceLocation: Original species description, Ecology; Mt. Kampalili paratypes
records.studyScope: Two paratype capture sites in the Mt. Kampalili upper montane forest, not a confirmed required microhabitat for all animals; specific rare-species locality coordinates withheld.

records.label: Historical earthworm-bait trap records
records.text: Two of the three original specimens were taken in traps baited with live earthworms; the authors suggested earthworms as possible prey but did not report stomach-content proof.
records.source: Rowsey et al. (2022), Journal of Mammalogy 103:1259–1277
records.sourceLocation: Original species description, Ecology; three collected voucher specimens
records.studyScope: Three historical voucher specimens, two caught with earthworm bait. Bait attraction does not confirm ingested diet, foraging frequency, population size or current occupancy.
